summary.en: One tiny word handles both unspecified quantities and possession.

body.en:
From season 1, episodes 1, 3 and 5.

Henri's first rule tells Claire to drink *du thé chaud* ('some hot tea'). Yet when he hands over *la porte du grenier* ('the door of the attic') or Étienne opens *cette lettre du propriétaire* ('this letter from the owner'), *du* does not mean 'some' at all.

In both uses, *du* merges *de* and masculine *le*. After a verb like drinking or serving, partitive *du* introduces an uncounted amount (*du thé*, *du pain*, *du beurre*). Between two nouns, contracted *du* links one thing to another ('of the', 'from the').

Never assign the English word 'some' automatically; check what comes right before *du* as well as the masculine noun after it.

On replay, contrast *du thé chaud* after a verb with *du grenier* and *du propriétaire* attached to a preceding noun.
